title: Self-organization of magnetic islands and zonal magnetic fields driven by slab microtearing modes in the absence of magnetic shear
abstract: Self-organization in collisional microtearing turbulence is investigated using gyrokinetic simulations in a slab geometry without equilibrium magnetic shear. Unlike magnetically driven conventional tearing instabilities, microtearing instabilities are driven by the electron temperature gradient. Electron temperature fluctuations are found to contain most of the gyrokinetic free energy. Although magnetic perturbations contribute little to the free energy, the magnetic field structure plays a crucial role in the nonlinear evolution of microtearing turbulence. Zonal magnetic fields emerge spontaneously through the nonlinear interaction between magnetic perturbations and electron temperature fluctuations. These zonal fields provide an effective magnetic shear that enables magnetic islands to form despite the absence of equilibrium magnetic shear. The electron temperature profile is flattened within the islands. This flattening reduces the instability drive and is expected to promote turbulence saturation.
